newsitem.title: USA: Latin debt stuck in mud as Mexican paper gains.
newsitem.headline: Latin debt stuck in mud as Mexican paper gains.

text.p: Late-summer torpidity stymied activity in the Latin American debt market on Monday, as players narrowly opted for Mexico over other Brady bonds, traders said.

With many Wall Street players on vacation until September and the British markets on holiday Monday, Brady bond trade remained somnolent, and dealers could foresee little relief until the release of U.S. economic data later in the week.
"It is stunning how quiet things have turned out to be," said Dan Peirce, chief strategist at Bank of Boston. "In our market there doesn't seem to be too many people around."
Mexican paper thrived amid the paucity of trades, as players seemed increasingly convinced of the country's economic recovery.
"I see a lot of people rotating portfolios, going to Mexico because all the surprises have been on the upside," said James Barrineau, debt analyst at Smith Barney.
"You have upside growth surprises, inflation continuing to come down and the other markets cooperating such that money is going to go to Mexico," Barrineau added.
The Mexican Cetes rate continued its path lower, closing at 22.5 percent, its level since December 1994.
